title: Design, computational profiling, synthesis and biological evaluation of novel 1,2,4-triazole based derivatives as antioxidant and potent p53-MDM2 inhibitors.
authors: Kotadiya, Dushyant D; Thakur, Pooja S; Nair, Ruchi; Prajapati, Apurva; Patel, Dharmesh A; Patel, Siddharth S; Kumari, Shilpa; Priya, Kanu; Patel, Hitesh D
one_liner_zh: 该研究设计合成三唑类小分子作为p53-MDM2抑制剂，虽用分子对接和MD模拟，但对象是蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: Cancer remains the second leading cause of death globally, primarily because of the shortcomings of existing treatments, which include early drug resistance, metastasis, inadequate pharmacokinetics, and systemic toxicity. Small-molecule inhibitors that target the interaction of MDM2 and p53 show promise for reactivating p53 function and suppressing tumor growth. In this study, we designed, produced, and evaluated a number of 2-(4-((2,4-difluorobenzylidene)amino)-5-mercapto-4H-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl)phenol derivatives as possible anticancer agents utilizing both in silico and in vitro approaches. All obtained compounds showed effective binding interactions, as evidenced by their high docking scores. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations validated the structural stability, compactness, and rigidity of the most active molecule during a 100 ns time period. ADMET predictions indicated good pharmacokinetic parameters and low toxicity profiles, whereas DFT investigates validated the compounds' reactive features and electronic compatibility for biological activity. The structures of the synthesized compounds were confirmed through (1)H NMR, (13)C NMR, IR, and ESI-MS analyses. The anticancer activity in vitro was assessed using the MTT assay on MCF-7 and A549 cell lines. Of all the compounds tested, compound 8D, N-(benzo[d]thiazol-2-yl)-2-((4-((2,4-difluorobenzylidene)amino)-5-(2-hydroxyphenyl)-4H-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl)thio)acetamide, exhibited the strongest activity against MCF7 & A549 cells, with an IC(5)(0) value of 7.56 & 7.22 muM respectively. This study identifies a new class of small-molecule inhibitors that interact with p53 and MDM2, characterized by low toxicity and high efficacy, which could be turned into anticancer drugs. These findings are essential for medicinal chemists and researchers working on the discovery of anticancer medicines.
abstract_zh: 癌症仍然是全球第二大死亡原因，主要归因于现有治疗方法的缺陷，包括早期耐药性、转移、药代动力学不足和全身毒性。靶向MDM2与p53相互作用的小分子抑制剂在重新激活p53功能和抑制肿瘤生长方面显示出前景。在本研究中，我们设计、合成并评估了一系列2-(4-((2,4-二氟苄叉基)氨基)-5-巯基-4H-1,2,4-三唑-3-基)苯酚衍生物作为潜在抗癌剂，采用计算机模拟和体外方法。所有获得的化合物均显示出有效的结合相互作用，这由其高对接分数所证实。分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟验证了最具活性分子在100 ns时间内的结构稳定性、紧凑性和刚性。ADMET预测表明良好的药代动力学参数和低毒性特征，而DFT研究则验证了化合物的反应特性和电子兼容性以支持生物活性。合成化合物的结构通过(1)H NMR、(13)C NMR、IR和ESI-MS分析确认。体外抗癌活性使用MTT法在MCF-7和A549细胞系上评估。在所有测试化合物中，化合物8D，N-(苯并[d]噻唑-2-基)-2-((4-((2,4-二氟苄叉基)氨基)-5-(2-羟基苯基)-4H-1,2,4-三唑-3-基)硫代)乙酰胺，对MCF7和A549细胞表现出最强活性，其IC(5)(0)值分别为7.56和7.22 μM。本研究识别了一类新的与p53和MDM2相互作用的小分子抑制剂，具有低毒性和高效性，可能转化为抗癌药物。这些发现对于从事抗癌药物发现的药物化学家和研究人员至关重要。
